data.title: Starboard Value's top holding assigned Buy rating by Seeking Alpha's quant rating
data.description:
New York-based Starboard Value reported a third-quarter portfolio value of $4.67B, up 3% sequentially. Compared to the year-ago period, the portfolio value decreased 12% despite an increase in its holdings to 22 from 20.

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, Starboard’s top holdings remained unchanged, with iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF (IJH), Qorvo, and Kenvue continuing to occupy the top three spots. 

The fund, however, cranked up its holdings in iShares to 12.20M shares from 8.88M in the previous quarter—accounting for 19% of its total holdings. Starboard also increased Riot Platforms (RIOT) holdings to 10.50M shares from 10.11M.

Meanwhile, the fund slashed its holdings in Dynatrace (DT), Match Group (MTCH), and News Corp (NWS), among others.

Here is a list of Starboard’s top 15 holdings with Seeking Alpha's quant ratings:

  • iShares (IJH): Quant Rating: 3.84, Buy

data.title: Google expands Project Genie with real-time editing of AI-generated worlds
data.description:
Google (GOOGL) is expanding access to Project Genie, an experimental AI tool that lets users create and explore interactive virtual worlds, adding real-time editing, audio, and longer exploration sessions.

The updated experience will be available to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, the company said Thursday.

The company said the technology remains experimental. "We are actively tackling key challenges such as camera latency, intricate physical interactions, real-time audio precision, and long-term scene permanence," Google said in its blogpost.

The update introduces access to Genie 4, Google's latest world model, which allows users to modify environments through text prompts while exploring them. Users can change weather conditions, add characters, or alter events as they move through a generated world. The model also generates audio, including background sounds and character dialogue, that changes with the scene.

Google is also extending the capabilities of Genie 3, allowing users to explore generated worlds for up to three minutes per session, compared with 60 seconds previously. Users can also link multiple worlds together and create environments using 360-degree panoramic images.

Google said generated video and audio include SynthID watermarks and that inputs and outputs are screened for safety.

data.title: Europe’s clean-energy push deepens dependence on Chinese technology
data.description:
Europe’s transition away from imported fossil fuels is creating a different overseas dependence: Chinese clean-energy equipment. Wind and solar generated more EU electricity than fossil fuels last year, but inexpensive Chinese technology is helping drive that expansion while squeezing European manufacturers, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.

For investors, Europe’s response could reshape competition across solar, batteries and wind power. Procurement preferences and subsidies may support domestic suppliers, while restrictions on cheaper imports could raise developers’ costs and slow installations. Policy decisions will help determine which businesses capture the transition’s growth.

China produces at least 80% of the world’s solar products and lithium-ion batteries. European wind-turbine manufacturers retain a stronger position, although they rely heavily on Chinese rare-earth magnets.

The EU has proposed favoring European-made solar panels, turbines and batteries in public contracts. Some governments also subsidize purchases of locally manufactured equipment, but substantial price differences make it difficult to change buying habits.

Chinese wind equipment costs 30% to 45% less to manufacture, while Chinese electrolyzers used to produce hydrogen can cost less than half their European equivalents. Protecting domestic production could therefore make Europe’s climate goals more expensive to achieve.

Security concerns are adding pressure for restrictions. The EU has barred Chinese inverters from EU-funded projects and is considering broader limits. These devices connect solar generation to usable electricity, and experts warn coordinated cyberattacks could disrupt power supplies.

Europe’s challenge is deciding which industries warrant support. Bruegel researcher Simone Tagliapietra argues that inexpensive solar imports have accelerated deployment and created installation jobs, while Europe could concentrate industrial investment in stronger businesses such as cables and wind turbines.

data.title: Skydance is combining the Warner Bros. and Paramount TV studios
data.description:
Skydance Corporation (SKYD) is already making major post-merger moves. The media giant announced that it will combine Warner Bros. Television and Paramount Television Studios into a single TV studio entity that will have more than 100 productions under its control. The new organization will be called Warner Bros. Television Studios and will launch early next year. 

The merged studio unit is being co-led by Channing Dungey (head of Warner Bros. Television Group) and Matt Thunell (president of Paramount Television Studios). Both will report to George Cheeks, who oversees Skydance's (SKYD) broader television operations.

As part of the same broader TV restructuring, Skydance (SKYD) has also folded its television animation assets (Warner Bros. Animation, Cartoon Network Studios, Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe, and Nickelodeon Animation Studios) into a single division called Skydance Television Animation.

The consolidation is a major piece of Skydance's (SKYD) post-merger integration strategy aimed at achieving $6B in annual synergies within three years. Separately, Skydance (SKYD) is considering combining Paramount+ and HBO Max into one streaming service.

Shares of Skydance (SKYD) are up about 2% since the mega-merger closed.

data.title: U.S. indexes are mixed after Nvidia earnings; gold declines
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages were mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia (NVDA) reported better-than-expected Q3 results amid the recent CEO scandal. Investor sentiment was shaken as they now turn to upcoming FOMC minutes from the last meeting.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was +0.8, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) was -0.7%.

Nvidia shares seesawed and were last -2.1% after the company reported Q3 results that showed a 75% year-over-year revenue growth estimate for the fiscal year ending January 2028.

“Nvidia earnings are a tech bellwether in the same way that GDP tells you what the economy was doing three months ago,” said Dario Perkins, managing director of Global Macro at TS Lombard.

“Technology is down to 35.4% of the S&P 500 and more than 19% off the recent highs. Still outperforming the S&P 500 YTD though,” Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group, added.

On the economic side, U.S. housing starts jumped 9.9% month-over-month in October, more than expected, while permits increased less than consensus anticipated. In addition, the October U.S. Pending Home Sales Index slid -4.7% this month, more than expected.

Later today, the Federal Reserve will release the minutes from its last meeting. Bank of America expects the minutes to reveal a deeper divide over the decision to be on rate hold than the 10-2 vote suggested.

The gold spot price (XAUUSD:CUR) is down 2.9% on Wednesday due to hawkish monetary policy expectations and the ongoing stock market weakness.

Over to the bond market, yields were lower. The 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) declined 6 basis points to 5.06%, while the 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) also was 3 basis points lower at 4.79%. The 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) was 5 basis points lower at 5.41%.

Oil prices were mostly lower. Crude oil futures (CL1:COM) were $82, while Brent (CO1:COM) was $91 per barrel.

data.title: Lyft adds 9% following CEO's appearance at RBC conference
data.description:
Shares of Lyft Inc. rose about 8% on Wednesday, a day after Chief Executive David Risher told investors at RBC Capital Markets’ Global Technology, Internet, Media and Telecommunications Conference that the ride-hailing company had made a “strong start to the quarter.” The stock rose $1.49 to reach $18.21 in afternoon trading.

Speaking Tuesday, Risher said the fourth quarter was going “possibly even slightly stronger than we expected,” though he told analysts not to change their models. He credited the momentum to rider incentives Lyft spent on in the third quarter, saying their effects were lasting weeks and months and were stronger than the company had expected. He also repeated that growth in Lyft’s North American rideshare business, which has accelerated for two straight quarters, “will accelerate again next quarter.”

data.title: Fervo Energy rises after signing 105 MW Utah transmission agreement
data.description:
Fervo Energy (FRVO) rose 3.8% in Wednesday's trading after saying it executed a new 105 MW transmission service agreement with Longroad Energy for development of the Cape Station geothermal project in Beaver County, Utah, where Fervo has been developing geothermal energy infrastructure.

Fervo (FRVO) said the deal gives it long-term, firm delivery rights on the Milford Gen Lead line and builds on the parties' existing 400 MW arrangement, raising Cape Station's total contracted long-term firm transmission capacity to 505 MW.

"Longroad has worked alongside Fervo since its first efforts in Beaver County, and we're excited to collaborate again," Longroad Energy's chief development officer said. "Providing transmission service for this next phase helps deliver clean, around-the-clock power to the grid."

The transmission service agreement is expected to begin in 2028, subject to regulatory approvals.

data.title: Tandem upgraded, Insulet downgraded at Stifel on market for tubeless insulin pumps
data.description:
Stifel upgraded Tandem Diabetes Care (TNDM) and downgraded its rival Insulet Corporation (PODD), citing results from a survey indicating the latest trends in the market for tubeless insulin pumps.

Analyst Jonathan Block upgraded Tandem (TNDM) to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $26 from $22, stating that the company’s recently authorized Mobi insulin pump could capture 28% of new customer starts in 2028 according to Stifel's survey of 52 physicians.

“Even a more modest level of share could help drive accelerating growth for Tandem in 2028 and beyond and more than offset tepid renewals,” Block wrote, noting that improving margins and the company’s recent shift to the pharmacy channel will act as additional tailwinds that can lift its multiple.

The analyst downgraded Insulet (PODD) to Hold from Buy, noting that while new competitors will help expand the market for tubeless pumps, it won’t be sufficient for the company to offset its anticipated losses in market share in 2028. 

"Our checks have tubeless accounting for 46% of new customer starts in 2026, and this increases to ~65% in 2028, a function of new offerings hitting the market," the analyst wrote. "However, Insulet’s share of the tubeless pie is expected to decline from 100% to less than 50%, which could result in declining y/y new customer starts in 2028,” Block wrote as he lowered his price target to $165 from $180 per share.
